key_insight: Variable-geometry sample-based quantum diagonalization (VGSQD) reuses quantum samples across molecular geometries, extending quantum chemistry calculations to geometry optimization and reaction pathways with reduced quantum computational cost.
engineering_relevance: Reusing samples could make hybrid quantum-classical workflows more practical for molecular structure and reaction studies relevant to catalysis and drug discovery.
method: Generate quantum samples at a reference molecular geometry.
Reuse those samples for SQD calculations at displaced geometries.
Use the resulting energies to optimize structures and trace reaction pathways.
evidence_signal: Using circuits of up to 124 qubits on IBM's ibm-quebec Heron r2 processor, the authors studied beryllium dimer and water equilibrium properties and a hydrogen exchange reaction pathway, reporting results comparable to CCSD(T) and DMRG.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify computational savings or establish how reliably reference-geometry samples transfer across larger structural changes.
paper_title: Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization for Variable Molecular Geometries
